title: kbjob.py follow prints one line per move of a job and exits with its result, so a Monitor or a background shell reports the end
goal: python3 _tools/kbjob.py [--store PATH] follow JOB [--since SEQ] [--timeout S] prints one line per job event of JOB from SEQ, flushed at once (JOB STATE OP SUBJECT [step=NAME] [exit=N]; never a line of the command's own output, which stays in the log), ends on a terminal state with the line JOB STATE exit=N log=PATH and exits 0 for succeeded, 1 for failed or refused, 3 for cancelled; with the default --timeout 1500 s (under the Monitor tool's effective deadline of 1800 s) it prints a last line follow: still running, continue with --since N and exits 4, so one more Monitor call or background shell resumes it without a missed move; status [JOB|--active] prints the job's JSON as kj_store.status gives it (or every job not terminal), log JOB [--tail N] prints the end of its output log, and cancel JOB moves a queued job to cancelled and a running one's process group to TERM then KILL and cancelled, for the submitting operator only (exit 1 for another's)

run: import sys,os,tempfile,subprocess; sys.path.insert(0,"_tools"); import kj_store; s=os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(),"c.sqlite"); a=kj_store.submit(".","check","","claude-0123abcd",{"name":"backlog-check"},store=s); j=a["job"]; co=lambda *x: subprocess.run([sys.executable,"_tools/coord.py","--store",s,*x],capture_output=True,text=True); fo=lambda *x: subprocess.run([sys.executable,"_tools/kbjob.py","--store",s,"follow",j,*x],capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=60); co("transition","job/"+j,"--to","running"); r=fo("--timeout","2"); assert r.returncode==4 and "--since" in r.stdout.splitlines()[-1], r; co("transition","job/"+j,"--to","refused","--field","exit=1","--field","step=rebase"); r=fo("--timeout","5"); lines=r.stdout.splitlines(); assert r.returncode==1 and lines[-1].startswith(j+" refused") and "step=rebase" in lines[-1], r

import sys,os,tempfile,subprocess; sys.path.insert(0,"_tools"); import kj_store; s=os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(),"c.sqlite"); a=kj_store.submit(".","check","","claude-0123abcd",{"name":"backlog-check"},store=s); j=a["job"]; kb=lambda *x: subprocess.run([sys.executable,"_tools/kbjob.py","--store",s,*x],capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=60); assert kb("cancel",j).returncode==0; assert kj_store.status(".",j,store=s)["state"]=="cancelled"; r=kb("follow",j,"--timeout","5"); assert r.returncode==3 and "cancelled" in r.stdout.splitlines()[-1], r; assert kb("status","--active").stdout.count(j)==0

JOB STATE exit=N log=PATH only, the step on the terminal event line above it

status --active prints one kj_store.status object per job; log prints the whole file

gates.question: How does cancel end a running job, given the job record holds no process id?
options: Find the executor from the lease jobrun/JOB (holder serve-PID), take its child that leads its own process group, move the job to cancelled, then TERM and after a grace KILL that group; POSIX hosts, the job's own host only
Add a pid field to the job record in kj_exec and kill by it

notes: Why a line per move and exit codes: Claude Code's Monitor tool runs a command and each stdout line reaches the session as an event, its exit ends the watch, timeout_ms defaults to 300000 and the effective deadline is at most 1800000 ms, persistent false (live docs, not in the kb: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/python#monitor, read 2026-11-08; kb: public/claude/hooks.md:212 DOC S-fksbud2r). A Bash command with run_in_background ends with a task notification at exit and, in a local interactive session, has no time limit, while unattended -p runs stop it at 30 min by default and 2 h at most (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#time-limit-for-background-commands, read 2026-11-08), and every background task dies when Claude Code exits (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode#how-backgrounding-works, read 2026-11-08): the job outlives the session because the executor, not the session's shell, owns it; follow only reads. Exit 4 with the since cursor makes a follow resumable across Monitor deadlines. follow prints no command output so a Monitor line never carries a path's content or a secret; the skill's current wait is coord.py wait --kind progress --item (kb-sprint SKILL.md:57), whose events follow reuses (coord wait --kind job). cancel is by the submitting operator only (authority rule). No test added (ceiling). Order agreed 2026-11-08 with SP-ep7ck2ab's manager (ask A1e21b0d155): shared kb/_self/map.csv rows land by first claim, the later item rebases; no hard dependency.
